To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) RNNs can outperform CNNs for emotion classification in video; 2) the combination of CNN and RNN features can outperform the best of either; and 3) the best results are obtained by using the CNN and RNN feature combination with the CNN features as the input to the RNN.

(i) a new hybrid CNN-RNN system for the EmotiW 2015 Challenge; (ii) a comparative analysis of the hybrid CNN-RNN approach with a previously applied CNN system; and (iii) an ablation study of the CNN-RNN architecture.

the application of RNNs for the recognition of emotion in video.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed hybrid CNN-RNN approach is the best-performing system for the EmotiW challenge and that it outperforms the previous state-of-the-art by a statistically significant margin on the 2015 test set.
the proposed hybrid architecture is a strong contender in the Emotion Recognition in The Wild Challenge and it is capable of outperforming the previously used CNN approach.
RNNs are a powerful tool for sequence analysis, and in particular for emotion recognition in the wild.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the first to use recurrent neural networks for emotion recognition in the wild.
we present the first end-to-end RNN approach to facial expression analysis and show that it outperforms a previously published CNN-based approach.
we present the first RNN based architecture for EmotiW and that we demonstrate its effectiveness by outperforming the previous best result on this dataset.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RNN architecture can provide a more powerful framework for the aggregation of information over a video sequence than the previously applied CNN approach.
RNNs provide a natural framework for the analysis of variable length video sequences.
RNNs can be used as a drop-in replacement for CNNs for temporal aggregation in facial expression analysis.
